parameters.name: filter[statuses]
parameters.description: Statuses of appointments to fetch. Options `0` - Pending `1` - Pending Client Approval `2` - Pending Clinic Approval `3` - Rescheduled Clinic Approval `4` - Rescheduled Client Approval `5` - Confirmed `6` - Canceled By Client `7` - Canceled By Clinic' `8` - Automatically Created' `9` - No Show

parameters.description: Same as `filter[date_between]`, but the supplied dates are interpreted as UTC rather than the clinic's timezone. Format: `YYYY-MM-DD,YYYY-MM-DD`.

parameters.name: filter[last_fetched]
parameters.description: Returns appointments whose `updated_at` is strictly greater than this moment. Use this for incremental sync: it catches appointments modified since your last poll regardless of when they are scheduled. Send an ISO-8601 datetime; include the offset or a `Z` suffix (e.g. `2026-06-21T00:00:00Z`) so the moment is unambiguous — a value without one is read in the clinic's timezone. `updated_at` has one-second resolution and the comparison is exclusive, so subtract a small overlap (a minute is plenty) from your last cursor rather than passing it verbatim, otherwise a change written in the same second as your previous poll can be skipped.

post.summary: Create a purchase order from an external provider payload
post.description:
Permissions needed: `CREATE_ORDERS`.

Imports a purchase order from an external provider payload (the same payload shape consumed by the Vetcove webhook), under standard API authentication.

The authenticated vet becomes the purchase order's vet. The target clinic is resolved from the auth context via the `X-ClinicId` header; when omitted it falls back to the authenticated vet's active clinic. The clinic is never read from the request body.

For each item the importer finds or creates the product (and its manufacturer/producer), computes `cogs` from `unit_price` and `units`, and creates the purchase order line. The supplier is matched or created from `supplier.name`. The created purchase order is returned synchronously with status `PENDING`, document type `INVOICE`, and series `EXTERNAL`.

post.summary: Confirm receipt of a Purchase Order
post.description:
Permissions needed: `EDIT_ORDERS`.

Marks a pending, draft or backorder purchase order as completed and adds its lines to the clinic's stock, exactly as completing the order in the app does. Quantities, costs and prices are never changed by this call; only the order status and each line's `is_received` flag.

Omit `items` (or send an empty body) to receive every line. To receive only some lines, list the ones that did not arrive with `is_received: false`; lines that are not listed count as received. A `finalization_strategy` is then required: `create_backorder` moves the unreceived lines to a new backorder purchase order (returned as `related_order`), `keep_unreceived` drops them from this order.

An order that is already completed is rejected with 422.
